genxml.title: SGI MC memory controller of the R4000 Indigo, Indy and Indigo2: CPU control, GIO arbitration, memory configuration, error reporting and the graphics DMA engine
genxml.doc: The MC gate array sits between the R4000, main memory and the GIO bus. This unit is every register software touches. Offsets are from the start of the MC window (physical 1fa00000) and are the big-endian view: the chip answers each register at two addresses four bytes apart, the higher one for a big-endian CPU and the lower one for a little-endian CPU (the lower is these offsets minus 4; the semaphore pages and the DMA block follow the same rule). All registers are 32-bit words on the CPU bus; the IRIX header marks some as byte or halfword registers, which says how many bits are meaningful, not a different access width. Grades: established means the public IRIX source tree, a shipped IRIX header or the MC chip specification states it; inferred means a reasoned reading, with the reasoning in devices/mc/README.md. The specification covers MC revisions A and B (Fast Forward machines, Indigo notes included); the Indigo board carries revisions A to C, so a reset value taken from the specification is graded for the specification's revision and is not a read of an Indigo.

struct.name: CPUCTRL0
struct.from: MC Chip Specification, section 5.1; IRIX sys/mc.h
struct.doc: CPU control 0: refresh, parity reporting, watchdog enable, system and graphics reset, interrupt enable, PROM-write bus error, warm resets, the little-endian toggle, the MUX FIFO high-water mark and the bus-error data stall. The Indigo PROM reads this register back after every store to any MC register, as a write-buffer flush, and the kernel's first-revision workaround is a dummy PROM read before each MC store. A qtest can check the reset value, that the stall field and the high-water field read back what was written, and that writing the warm-restart bit restarts the CPU without clearing memory.

struct.name: CPUCTRL1
struct.from: MC Chip Specification, section 5.2; IRIX sys/mc.h
struct.doc: CPU control 1: the CPU address/command FIFO high-water mark, GIO bus timeout enable and the fixed-endianness selects for the HPC and the two GIO slots. The HPC fixed bit must be set for an HPC1.5, which every Indigo uses, and clear for an HPC3. A qtest can check the reset value and that bits outside the defined ones read back as written or as zero (the source does not say which).

struct.name: DOGC
struct.from: MC Chip Specification, section 5.3; IRIX sys/mc.h
struct.doc: Watchdog timer. A read returns the 20-bit counter, which counts refresh bursts and so wraps in about 67 seconds at the 62 microsecond refresh interval; any write clears it. When CPUCTRL0 enables the watchdog, a wrap resets the machine. IRIX names the read and the write DOGC and DOGR.

struct.name: SYSID
struct.from: MC Chip Specification, section 5.4; IRIX sys/mc.h
struct.doc: MC revision and EISA-present bit. The specification gives revision A as 0 and revision B as 1; IRIX code treats revisions 0 and 1 specially and refers to a 'revision C' part for large DRAM, which is inferred to read 3.

struct.name: RPSS_DIVIDER
struct.from: MC Chip Specification, section 5.5; IRIX sys/mc.h
struct.doc: Divider and increment for the RPSS counter. The counter adds the increment each time the CPU clock has been divided by the divider plus one. At a 50 MHz CPU clock the reset value (divide by five, add one) counts every 100 nanoseconds; for a 33 MHz clock the specification says divide by ten and add three. IRIX kernels write a different value (divide by two, add one).

struct.name: EEROM
struct.from: MC Chip Specification, section 5.6; IRIX sys/mc.h
struct.doc: Bit-banged serial interface to the 93C56-class EEPROM that holds the R4000 mode stream. The first three EEPROM bits are read by the MC itself at reset: byte order, HPC bus width and a reserved bit. Software rewrites the EEPROM through this register and then restarts the CPU to change byte order. The data-in bit cannot be written. A qtest can check that data-in follows the modelled EEPROM and that chip-select and clock read back.

field.name: pre
field.from: Linux asm/sgi/mc.h names it as the EEPROM PRE pin; the specification and the IRIX header call it reserved

struct.name: CTRLD
struct.from: MC Chip Specification, section 5.7; IRIX sys/mc.h
struct.doc: Refresh counter preload. The counter counts down at the CPU clock and, on reaching zero, reloads from this register and requests a refresh burst. It should hold the number of CPU clocks in 62.5 microseconds.

struct.name: REF_CTR
struct.from: MC Chip Specification, section 5.8; IRIX sys/mc.h
struct.doc: Current value of the refresh counter.

struct.name: GIO64_ARB
struct.from: MC Chip Specification, section 5.9; IRIX sys/mc.h
struct.doc: GIO arbitration parameters: per-device bus width, real-time or long-burst class, bus-master ability and pipelining. Real-time devices are served in fixed priority; long-burst devices round-robin with the CPU between each. The IRIX kernel comments that reads of this register and of the two time registers can return corrupted values, so it writes from a software copy and never reads back. A qtest can check the reset value and that every defined bit stores.

struct.name: CPU_TIME
struct.from: MC Chip Specification, section 5.10; IRIX sys/mc.h
struct.doc: Length of the CPU's arbitration slot in GIO clocks. The CPU holds the bus for the whole period even if idle. IRIX writes 43 (about 1.3 microseconds at 33 MHz).

struct.name: LB_TIME
struct.from: MC Chip Specification, section 5.11; IRIX sys/mc.h
struct.doc: Length of the long-burst devices' arbitration slot in GIO clocks. Unlike the CPU's, a long-burst slot ends when the device stops using the bus. IRIX writes 847 (about 25 microseconds at 33 MHz).

struct.name: MEMCFG0
struct.from: MC Chip Specification, section 5.12; IRIX sys/mc.h and the IRIX kernel's bank code
struct.doc: Memory configuration for banks 0 (high half) and 1 (low half). Each bank is four 36-bit SIMMs of one size. The base is compared with physical address bits 29 to 22, so it is in 4 MiB units and must be a multiple of the bank size; larger banks go at lower bases. A zero half means no usable bank. The specification gives only the valid bits a reset value of 0. If two valid banks overlap, accesses raise a bus error and do not complete.

struct.name: MEMCFG1
struct.from: MC Chip Specification, section 5.12; IRIX sys/mc.h and the IRIX kernel's bank code
struct.doc: Memory configuration for banks 2 (high half) and 3 (low half); the layout is that of the first configuration register.

struct.name: CPU_MEMACC
struct.from: MC Chip Specification, section 5.13; IRIX sys/mc.h
struct.doc: DRAM timing used for CPU accesses, in CPU clocks. The Indigo PROM writes 0x11453433 and tests the register by walking a one bit through the low 28 bits, then restoring the old value. A qtest can check the reset value and that bits 27 to 0 store.

struct.name: GIO_MEMACC
struct.from: MC Chip Specification, section 5.13; IRIX sys/mc.h
struct.doc: DRAM timing used for GIO accesses, in GIO clocks. The specification recommends write and read column 2, row 3 and precharge 2; the Indigo PROM writes read column 3, the Indy and Indigo2 PROMs read column 2.

struct.name: CPU_ERR_ADDR
struct.from: MC Chip Specification, section 5.14; IRIX sys/mc.h
struct.doc: Address of the last CPU parity or bus error; valid only while an error bit is set in the CPU error status. For a parity error the low three bits are meaningless and the status byte field gives the failing byte lane. The specification's revision B fix list says revision A could latch the wrong address when a write follows a read that failed parity.

struct.name: CPU_ERR_STAT
struct.from: MC Chip Specification, section 5.15; IRIX sys/mc.h
struct.doc: CPU error status. Any write clears it (the PROM and the kernel write zero). The bits are sticky. A qtest can check that a write of any value clears every bit and that a CPU read of an unmapped address sets the address-error bit.

struct.name: GIO_ERR_ADDR
struct.from: MC Chip Specification, section 5.16; IRIX sys/mc.h
struct.doc: Address of the last GIO parity or bus error, valid while a GIO error bit is set. Low two bits are meaningless for 32-bit devices, low three for 64-bit.

struct.name: GIO_ERR_STAT
struct.from: MC Chip Specification, section 5.17; IRIX sys/mc.h
struct.doc: GIO error status. Any write clears it. The bits are sticky.

struct.name: SYS_SEMAPHORE
struct.from: MC Chip Specification, sections 2.6.1 and 5.18; IRIX sys/mc.h
struct.doc: System semaphore, in the privileged register page. A read returns the bit and sets it to one; a write stores bit 0.

struct.name: LOCK_MEMORY
struct.from: MC Chip Specification, section 5.19; IRIX sys/mc.h
struct.doc: Writing 0 locks every device except the CPU out of main memory, for a locked CPU sequence; 1 releases.

struct.name: EISA_LOCK
struct.from: MC Chip Specification, section 5.20; IRIX sys/mc.h
struct.doc: Writing 0 asserts the EISA lock output. The Indigo has no EISA bus, so the register has no effect there (inferred from the absent bus).

struct.name: DMA_GIO_MASK
struct.from: IRIX sys/mc.h (name and role); IRIX VDMA initialisation (writes zero)
struct.doc: Mask applied to the GIO address of a graphics DMA to translate it, with the substitution register. The kernel and the Indigo PROM store zero in both, which leaves the address unchanged. The bit layout is not stated by any source held.

struct.name: DMA_GIO_SUB
struct.from: IRIX sys/mc.h (name and role); IRIX VDMA initialisation (writes zero)
struct.doc: Substitution bits for the GIO address translation; see the mask register.

struct.name: DMA_CAUSE
struct.from: IRIX VDMA header and kernel VDMA code; IRIX sys/mc.h
struct.doc: Sticky cause bits of the graphics DMA engine, the same bits the run register shows below the running bit. Software writes zero to clear them and to drop the DMA-done interrupt. Whether a write of any value clears them is not stated; IRIX only writes zero.

struct.name: DMA_CTL
struct.from: IRIX VDMA header and kernel VDMA code
struct.doc: Graphics DMA control. The kernel initialises it to a constant that also carries fields no source names (the kernel's comment lists a TLB limit of 512, a slave limit of 4, a 32-word cache line and the page size); only the three named bits are defined here. The Indigo PROM writes zero to turn translation off for its memory-clear DMA.

struct.name: DMA_TLB_HI
struct.from: IRIX kernel VDMA code (uTLB handling)
struct.doc: DMA TLB entry high word, four entries. Holds the virtual address of one segment (the span one page of page-table entries maps), aligned to that span. Software clears unused entries by writing zero.

struct.name: DMA_TLB_LO
struct.from: IRIX kernel VDMA code (uTLB handling)
struct.doc: DMA TLB entry low word, four entries. Names the physical page of page-table entries for the segment in the matching high word. Bits 25 to 6 are the physical address divided by 64.

struct.name: RPSS_CTR
struct.from: MC Chip Specification, sections 2.6.2 and 5.21; IRIX sys/mc.h
struct.doc: RPSS counter: 32 bits, read only, rolls over without an interrupt. It advances by the divider register's increment every divider-plus-one CPU clocks; at reset that is one every 100 nanoseconds at 50 MHz. The page is mappable by user processes. A qtest can check that two reads differ and that a write is ignored.

struct.name: DMA_MEMADR
struct.from: IRIX sys/mc.h; IRIX kernel VDMA code
struct.doc: DMA memory address, virtual or physical according to the translate bit. It advances as the DMA runs, so after a stop or fault it names the next byte; software reads it to find the faulting address.

struct.name: DMA_MEMADRD
struct.from: IRIX sys/mc.h (name and note: memory address and set defaults)
struct.doc: Writes the memory address register and also sets default values for the other DMA parameters. Which defaults is not stated by any source held, and no held code writes it.

struct.name: DMA_SIZE
struct.from: IRIX kernel VDMA code; Indigo PROM memory clear
struct.doc: DMA line width in bytes and line count. The kernel splits transfers over 65535 bytes into lines of 32768.

struct.name: DMA_STRIDE
struct.from: IRIX kernel VDMA code; IRIX vdma_args structure
struct.doc: Signed byte distance from the end of one line to the start of the next, and the vertical zoom factor (how many times each line repeats, at most 1023). The kernel forces the stride to zero when there is one line to avoid a TLB-miss quirk.

struct.name: DMA_GIO_ADR
struct.from: IRIX sys/mc.h; IRIX vdma_args structure
struct.doc: GIO slave address of the DMA, or the constant to write in fill mode. Writing it does not start the DMA.

struct.name: DMA_GIO_ADRS
struct.from: IRIX sys/mc.h; IRIX kernel VDMA code; Indigo PROM memory clear
struct.doc: Writes the GIO address (or fill constant) and starts the DMA. The kernel writes it last, after the other parameters.

struct.name: DMA_MODE
struct.from: IRIX VDMA header
struct.doc: DMA mode. The Indigo PROM's memory clear uses long burst, incrementing address, fill and graphics-to-host.

struct.name: DMA_COUNT
struct.from: IRIX sys/mc.h (name: zoom count and byte count); Indigo PROM memory clear
struct.doc: Working counters of the running DMA: the remaining zoom count and byte count. The Indigo PROM writes 1 in the upper half before starting a fill, commenting that the zoom factor is one; the field layout is not stated by any source held.

struct.name: DMA_STDMA
struct.from: IRIX kernel VDMA code
struct.doc: Start or resume the virtual DMA. The kernel writes 1 after fixing a page fault to resume and 0 to stop a timed-out transfer.

struct.name: DMA_RUN
struct.from: IRIX VDMA header and kernel VDMA code; Indigo PROM memory clear
struct.doc: DMA status: the cause bits plus a running bit. The PROM polls the running bit to wait for its memory clear.

struct.name: DMA_MEMADRDS
struct.from: IRIX sys/mc.h (name and note: memory address, set defaults and start DMA)
struct.doc: Writes the memory address, sets the default DMA parameters and starts the DMA. No held code writes it.

struct.name: SEMAPHORE
struct.from: MC Chip Specification, sections 2.6.1 and 5.18; IRIX sys/mc.h
struct.doc: Sixteen user semaphores, each in its own 4 KiB page so a page can be mapped into a user process. A read returns the bit and sets it to one; a write stores bit 0.
